C. Adverse Impacts Which Cannot be Avoided Should the Proposal be Implemented.
As listed and discussed under B, on the basis of our assessment of current knowledge of the Ross Ice Shelf and its subtending water and sediments, we anticipate no intentional impacts of great magnitude, longevity or importance. The majority of the impacts will be short-term and extremely localized, such as those associated with the camp and small laboratory facility on the Ross Ice Shelf during the period of drilling. These impacts will be monitored throughout the RISP operations. The surface should be restored within one year.
Functional activities at the project camp site will leave residual materials in the firn and ice which are not practical or possible to remove. These include contents of the sewage disposal pit, ash from solid waste incineration, drill hole casing and miscellaneous tools and materials which are inadvertently lost or buried. None of these have any direct environmental impact but will render the particular local area unsuitable for certain further scientific investigations of the <u>in-situ</u> firn and ice. Surficial evidence of site occupation will be non-existent in a short time, probably in less than a year, due to accumulation of new and drifting snow. Sufficient markers will be established to permit future identification.
